narrator.instruct: Fast-paced, energetic, punchy explainer narrator. Brisk delivery with no long pauses.

buddy.instruct: Outraged young guy at the movies, loud and cocky, whispering-shouting.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You just paid nine dollars for a bucket of popcorn.

lines.speaker: buddy
lines.text: Nine bucks? That's robbery. I brought my own.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your friend's jacket is stuffed with gas station candy. He feels like a genius.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He paid for his ticket, so the theater still got paid, right?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then a man in a suit walks into the box office and takes half the cash.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's the studio. About half of every ticket goes to whoever made the movie.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Some deals take upwards of seventy percent.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the ticket barely pays for the building, the staff, or the giant screen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But the snack counter? The studio gets none of that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Out of every snack dollar, the food itself costs about seventeen cents.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Snacks bring in only a fifth of the money, but around forty percent of the profit.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And after all that, the whole theater keeps about four cents per dollar.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's why theaters keep tickets low and popcorn high.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every overpriced bucket is quietly paying for your seat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your friend didn't beat the studio. The studio already got paid.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He just skipped the only part that keeps the lights on.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next week, someone new pays nine dollars for popcorn.
